stories.label: Top US and Russian diplomats discuss Ukraine war in Manila
stories.summary: Lavrov used the ASEAN summit to lay out Moscow's terms on Ukraine, the war on Iran, and nuclear proliferation while Rubio worked the same room. The value is the three-way perspective split — read the RU, QA and TR framings against each other. Lead with what the sit-down signals about where the war's diplomacy stands, not the boilerplate; the mechanism is ASEAN becoming the neutral venue where Washington and Moscow still talk.

stories.label: India's Modi promises fast-track courts for exam fraud fuelling protests
stories.summary: Modi's first public response to the youth-led exam-fraud protests: a promise of fast-track courts, echoed by Amit Shah. The surprise buried underneath — the same day the CBI said it found no evidence tying the alleged NEET-UG kingpin to the paper leak, undercutting the accountability the courts are meant to deliver. Lead with the gap between the political gesture and the collapsing case; this advances the protest arc with a genuine development.

stories.label: EXCLUSIVE: Permanent Secretary blocks release of funds approved by Tinubu for agencies
stories.summary: A permanent secretary allegedly froze funds Tinubu personally approved for information-ministry agencies — as retaliation because the agency heads refused to appear before her. The reveal is the mechanism of bureaucratic capture: a career official weaponizing payment files for personal deference, overriding a presidential directive. Accountability story from a Nigerian outlet on how state money actually moves.

stories.label: Five paramilitary troops killed in ambush at security checkpoint in Thailand
stories.summary: Six black-clad attackers hit a checkpoint in Narathiwat's Ra-ngae district with firearms and pipe bombs, killing five paramilitaries and wounding six civilians. The under-reported context to surface: the two-decade Malay-Muslim insurgency in Thailand's deep south, one of Asia's most persistent and least-covered conflicts. Lead with the toll and the district, then the structural grievance driving it.

stories.label: Burnham announces cut to business rates for pubs and clubs
stories.summary: New PM Andy Burnham's £100mn-a-year business-rates cut for pubs, clubs and music venues is the latest in a rapid-fire blitz of giveaways aimed at voters. The mechanism to examine: a '20% cut, fully funded' claim resting on an unspecified review — who actually pays. Burnham is spiking in public attention (top-read on Wikipedia); treat that as a signal readers want to understand his early fiscal moves.

stories.label: Pakistan 'disappointed' with EU report on GSP+ compliance issues, says it understates reforms
stories.summary: The EU's GSP+ assessment flagged Pakistan's compliance gaps on the human-rights and governance conventions that underpin its duty-free access to European markets; Islamabad calls the report an understatement of its reforms. The mechanism to teach: how trade preferences are quietly conditioned on rights performance, and what billions in textile exports ride on Brussels' verdict. Dawn carries the Pakistani government's side.

stories.label: South Korea's Korbit exchange is now part of the $1 trillion Mirae Group family
stories.summary: Mirae Asset — a trillion-dollar traditional-finance group — becomes the largest shareholder of Korbit, South Korea's first homegrown crypto exchange (est. 2013). The structural shift to lead with: legacy asset managers absorbing the crypto rails they once shunned, folding exchanges into regulated TradFi balance sheets. Frame it as the quiet institutionalization of crypto in a major Asian market.

stories.label: Extreme heat and flooding put millions at risk across the US as Tokyo hospitalizes hundreds
stories.summary: More than 100 million Americans fall under heat watches this week while Tokyo rushed over 260 people to hospitals in one day — the same intensifying-heatwave pattern on two continents. Lead with the twin numbers and the mechanism: compounding heat-plus-flood risk and the widening gap between where cooling infrastructure exists and where the heat is now landing. Distinct from the earlier France heat story.

stories.label: ONERA Selects AMOS to Build French Space Surveillance Telescope
stories.summary: France's ONERA tapped Belgium's AMOS to build PROVIDENCE, a 2.5m ground telescope that will image satellites in low Earth orbit for the French Air and Space Force by 2029. The teachable shift: space is now a surveilled military domain, and Europe is building dedicated optics to watch what flies overhead. Lead with the capability — tracking and imaging other nations' satellites — not the procurement.

stories.label: Bitcoin, Ethereum-linked protocols lose $35 million in multiple attacks hours apart
stories.summary: Two hacks hours apart — B² Network (~$3.86M via a seized staking-contract upgrade key) and Arbitrum's AFX Trade ($24M drained after bridge keys were compromised) — drove ~$35M in crypto losses in a day. The mechanism for developer readers: it's compromised keys and permissions, not broken cryptography, that keep bleeding these protocols, and AI-driven intrusion tooling is making key theft faster. Lead with the pattern, not either single theft.

stories.label: Judge approves $1.5B Anthropic settlement for pirated books used to train Claude
stories.summary: A judge signed off on Anthropic's $1.5B settlement over pirated books used to train Claude — the largest AI copyright payout yet, and a de facto price tag on scraped training data. The precedent to draw out: what this sets as the market rate for ingesting copyrighted work, and how it reshapes every frontier lab's data pipeline. Reader is a developer who understands training corpora; lead with the number and the precedent.

stories.label: What Happened When Flock Came to My Town
stories.summary: [Auto-backfill for tech floor] My small town in South Carolina will soon have more Flock cameras than police officers.

stories.label: Israel Firebombed a Family Home Where Children Were Sleeping in Latest Killing Spree
stories.summary: While global attention is on the renewed US-Iran war, Israel killed nearly 60 Palestinians in a week and moved to occupy ~70% of Gaza. Lead with the named victims — children firebombed while sleeping — and the structural why: the world's distraction is the cover under which the occupation advances. Continuation of the siege IS the development. Drop Site is doing original ground reporting no wire is carrying; count Palestinian dead with dignity and name the actor.

stories.label: The Protests Gripping India — and Rattling Modi
stories.summary: The NEET exam-leak scandal and student suicides have metastasized into the largest street challenge to Modi's authority in years. Lead with the shift the reader will grasp: what began as a single-issue grievance now channels broad frustration and may be a turning point for Indian politics. This is the structural sequel to the NEET paper-leak coverage — not the leak itself but the mass movement it detonated. Who is affected: a generation of students; who holds power: a government that suppressed the scandal.

stories.label: Houthis Now Attacking Saudi Oil Tankers In Red Sea, Major Energy Supply Implications
stories.summary: As the Iran war reignites, the Houthis have declared a Red Sea blockade and begun striking Saudi oil tankers — opening a second chokepoint while Hormuz is already all but closed. Lead with the mechanism: Riyadh diverts ~5M bpd through its East-West pipeline to Yanbu on the Red Sea, and that lone export outlet is now under fire. This compounds the Bab al-Mandeb/Hormuz squeeze the reader has been tracking; explain how two chokepoints closing at once multiplies global tanker and insurance costs, not just adds to them.

stories.label: Mexican journalist shot dead in Oaxaca, marking fourth such killing since June
stories.summary: Leyva, 60, who reported on government corruption and cartel violence, is the fourth Mexican journalist killed since June. Lead with the pattern, not the single death: a country where exposing power is now a fatal profession, and a state prosecutor's office investigating killings its own institutions rarely solve. Accountability angle — name the impunity mechanism (Special Prosecutor for Crimes Against Freedom of Expression that produces few convictions). Latin America as actor, not backdrop.

stories.label: China Coast Guard Exercises 'Jurisdiction' in Japan's Exclusive Economic Zone
stories.summary: China's Coast Guard has formally claimed to be 'exercising jurisdiction' inside Japan's EEZ — a rhetorical escalation that converts a patrol into a sovereignty assertion. Lead with the precedent: language, not just ships, is how maritime claims harden. The reader thinks in power shifts — this is Beijing testing whether Tokyo formulates a response or lets the framing stand, the same salami-slicing playbook seen against Manila. Consequence lies in what a non-response would concede.

stories.label: Pakistan thought it won the peace. Now, it could be dragged into war.
stories.summary: Pakistan brokered the US-Iran MoU and looked like the war's biggest winner; four weeks later the deal is dead and its defense pacts with Saudi Arabia (and now Kuwait talks) could drag it into a war its parliament refused to join in 2015. Lead with the economic trap: on its 25th IMF program, >50% of tax revenue servicing debt, Hormuz's closure already forcing four-day work weeks — Islamabad mediated to protect its own grid, and the war's restart has reopened every front it tried to close. Name the cost of disappointing any single Gulf patron: the UAE recalled $3.5B and deported Shia workers. Analysis synthesizing well-reported events, not an unsourced scoop.

stories.label: Can Cuba outlast Marco Rubio?
stories.summary: A congressional delegation calls Cuba's US-engineered fuel embargo a 'silent Gaza' — near-weekly nationwide blackouts, shuttered schools and hospitals running on fumes. Lead with the accountability mechanism the reader will find striking: as sanctions force fire-sale privatizations of Cuban state assets, Trump-linked investors (a former adviser buying a nickel/cobalt stake, Gulf figures advising on a 'Trump Island') are positioned to buy in — regime change reframed as a distressed-asset play. Firsthand reporting from a decade on the island; ẓulm with named actors on both the harm and the profit side.

stories.label: BTC wilts as Clarity Act odds tumble. U.S. deploys B1 bomber against Iran
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell below $66K as prediction markets priced the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act's passage odds down to 38% — Senate Democrats panning the latest draft — while rising oil and Treasury yields from the Iran war compounded the selloff. Lead with the linkage the reader will value: crypto's price now trades on the same two variables as everything else — US regulatory gridlock and a war-driven oil/rates shock. The mechanism, not the ticker, is the story: a 'digital gold' moving in lockstep with macro risk.

stories.label: New blood test speeds childhood cancer diagnosis
stories.summary: A liquid-biopsy blood test for Burkitt lymphoma — the most common childhood cancer in equatorial Africa — proved quick and accurate in East African studies, replacing invasive tissue biopsies that are slow or unavailable where oncologists are scarce. Lead with the equity mechanism: a diagnostic that works from a blood draw closes the gap for children who otherwise die undiagnosed. Global South science as the subject, not the recipient.

stories.label: Orcas filmed making sunfish explode by ramming them at high speed
stories.summary: In the Gulf of California, researchers documented a never-before-described orca behavior: ramming one of the world's heaviest bony fish at speed until it bursts, apparently teaching juveniles to break prey into edible pieces — and possibly for play. Lead with the specific, vivid detail and the open question of culture transmission in cetaceans. A palate-cleanser with real science: novel foraging behavior, a distinct population's learned tactic.

stories.label: Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber
stories.summary: Google shipped a tranche of Gemini Flash models — including a 'Flash Cyber' variant explicitly tuned for security work. Lead with what the reader (a developer) will care about: the segmentation strategy — cheap Flash-Lite for volume, a dedicated cyber model — signals where the frontier labs think the money and the risk are. Note the 'Cyber' framing: a general-purpose model marketed for offensive/defensive security is itself the news, not just a benchmark bump.

stories.label: How an AI research tool helped challenge support for police violence in Brazil
stories.summary: In a country that recorded 45,747 intentional violent deaths in 2023, researchers used an AI tool to probe why large publics endorse state violence — and to design counter-messaging. Lead with the applied mechanism: AI turned on the problem of manufactured consent for police killings, in the Global South, by local researchers. The reader gets both the tech (how the tool works) and the stakes (public opinion as the enabler of extrajudicial force). Accountability plus AI, non-Western subject.

stories.label: ASEAN's digital economy rulebook is nearly written
stories.summary: ASEAN is close to finalizing its Digital Economy Framework Agreement — the first region-wide rulebook for cross-border data, e-payments and digital trade among 10 states with wildly different regimes. Lead with the stakes for a bloc of 680M people: whoever sets the interoperability standards shapes a decade of digital growth, and the contest is between ASEAN self-determination and outside powers (US, China, Australia) angling to influence the terms. Structural, non-Western, and the kind of standards-setting story that decides who captures value.

stories.label: US judge sets 2027 trial date for Venezuela's Maduro
stories.summary: Nicolás Maduro and his wife, seized by the US military in January and jailed in Brooklyn, will not stand trial until June 2027 — nearly 18 months in US custody before a court hears the drug-trafficking charges. Lead with the mechanism the reader will find striking: a sitting head of state was captured by a foreign military and now sits in a Brooklyn jail awaiting a domestic US trial, a precedent for how Washington treats governments it seeks to remove. Note the Al Jazeera framing versus the US framing. Multi-source (US, IN, SG, QA).

stories.label: Why a Tibetan Protester Set Himself on Fire Outside the United Nations
stories.summary: Loga Rangzen's self-immolation outside the UN was meant to force Tibet back onto the international agenda; instead it exposed how thoroughly China's global influence has pushed the cause off it. Lead with the human act and the structural why: how Beijing's economic leverage has made governments and institutions quietly drop Tibet. The reader thinks in terms of power shifts — this is a case study in how a diaspora loses its diplomatic footing as a rival's clout grows. Single-source but a unique, systemic angle no wire is carrying.

stories.label: 3 killed, 5 injured as gunmen attack passenger bus in Balochistan's Mastung
stories.summary: Gunmen killed three and wounded five on a Karachi-bound bus while a bridge explosion severed the Quetta-Karachi highway for hours. Lead with the compounding pattern: coordinated attacks on transport and infrastructure in Balochistan are choking the province's connection to the rest of Pakistan, not just claiming individual lives. Name the victims and the mechanism — insurgency-by-attrition on the arteries that bind a marginalized province to the state. Regional primary source (Dawn, PK).

stories.label: Global trade up 12.5% amid Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions -- UNCTAD
stories.summary: UNCTAD reports global trade grew 12.5% in H1 2026 — but the agency says the rise is mostly higher prices, not more goods moving. Lead with that distinction: a headline 'growth' number that actually measures the inflation the Hormuz disruption is imposing on every importer. Teach the reader to read past the aggregate — this is a war tax dressed up as trade expansion, and the developing economies that import fuel and food bear it. Single-source (TASS citing UNCTAD data).

stories.label: Report: Pakistan Asks U.S. for $10 Billion 'Stabilization Fund'
stories.summary: Pakistan's finance minister reportedly asked the US Treasury for a $10bn currency-stabilization facility, banking on goodwill from Islamabad's mediation role in the US-Iran war. Lead with the mechanism: Pakistan is trying to convert diplomatic service into balance-of-payments relief — monetizing geopolitics because its reserves can't withstand another Hormuz-driven shock. The reader grasps the dependency trap: a 25th-IMF-program economy now seeking a bilateral backstop from the very power whose war is squeezing it. Regional source (Dawn, PK) carried through on the Bessent-Aurangzeb meeting.

stories.label: Khatam al-Anbia warns US against attacking infrastructure
stories.summary: Iran's top military command answered Trump's threat to bomb Iranian bridges and power plants with its own: if US threats are carried out, not a single drop of oil will leave the Gulf. Lead with the escalation ladder this completes — the reader saw Washington's reprisal doctrine; here is Tehran's counter, an explicit threat to weaponize the world's energy supply. Give the Iranian side symmetrically. The mechanism to teach: mutual infrastructure-targeting as coercion, with global oil markets as the hostage. Regional source (Mehr, IR).

stories.label: New study supports testing of Merck's Ebola vaccine in DRC outbreak
stories.summary: New human data suggests Merck's Ervebo — licensed only against the Zaire ebolavirus — may also protect against the different species now driving a rapidly expanding outbreak in the DRC. Lead with the stakes: a vaccine already in the field might work off-label against the strain actually spreading, which could reshape the response if regulators allow it. Teach the immunological why (cross-protection between ebolavirus species) and the accountability angle: who decides whether a licensed tool gets deployed against an unlicensed target while an outbreak grows.

stories.label: Iron-loaded biochar enhances electron shuttle function to promote paddy soil dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium
stories.summary: Researchers show iron-loaded biochar acts as an electron shuttle in rice paddies, pushing soil to retain nitrogen as ammonium instead of losing it to denitrification. Lead with why a farmer in the Global South should care: this is a cheap, char-based way to keep fertilizer nitrogen in the soil, cutting both input costs and emissions. Teach the mechanism simply — biochar moving electrons to change which chemical pathway wins — and the stakes for food systems that can't afford synthetic-fertilizer waste.

stories.label: Genomic population structure and adaptation of eastern Mediterranean loggerhead (Caretta caretta) nesting areas
stories.summary: Genome-scale analysis of eastern Mediterranean loggerhead turtles maps how distinct nesting populations — many on Turkish and Levantine coasts — are genetically adapting as the sea warms. Lead with the conservation stakes: knowing which nesting sites hold unique adaptive variation tells managers which beaches are irreplaceable under climate change. Teach the idea that biodiversity loss isn't just fewer animals — it's the erasure of local genetic adaptations a warming Mediterranean will need.

stories.label: Advertise in ChatGPT
stories.summary: OpenAI has opened an advertising business inside ChatGPT — the moment the dominant AI assistant crosses from subscription tool to ad-funded attention platform. Lead with what changes for the reader who uses it daily: once answers are monetized, the incentive shifts from being useful to being sponsorable, and the line between response and placement blurs. Teach the structural why — the same ad-model gravity that reshaped search now pulls on generative AI. High public attention (1,000+ HN points) confirms developers grasp the stakes.

stories.label: ISPs' long nightmare of having to list all the fees they charge is finally over
stories.summary: The FCC voted to scrap a Biden-era rule that forced ISPs to disclose all 'passthrough' fees on broadband price labels — restoring the industry's ability to advertise artificially low prices. Lead with the accountability inversion: a transparency requirement built to stop bill-shock has been repealed at the industry's request. Name who benefits (the carriers) and who pays (every subscriber who can no longer compare true prices). The mechanism to teach: how a quiet regulatory rollback re-legalizes hidden fees.

stories.label: Extension of CISA 2015 info-sharing protections passes as part of House's defense bill
stories.summary: A 10-year renewal of the CISA 2015 cyber threat-sharing law rode through the House inside the 2027 defense authorization bill. Lead with the mechanism the reader should notice: a consequential surveillance-adjacent law — the legal shield that lets companies hand threat data (and the user data attached) to government without liability — was renewed not on its own merits but bolted to a must-pass military bill. Teach why attaching civil-liberties-relevant law to the NDAA blunts scrutiny, and what a decade-long extension locks in.

stories.label: The U.S. Has Rules for Nuclear Deals With Other Countries. Here's How They Work.
stories.summary: Trump is set to grant Saudi Arabia a civilian nuclear program under a so-called 123 Agreement. Lead with the tension the deal papers over: Riyadh has long resisted the standard no-enrichment, no-reprocessing terms that these agreements exist to enforce, and doing this amid an active US-Iran war reshapes non-proliferation norms across the Gulf. Teach the mechanism — a 123 Agreement is the legal gate that decides whether a nuclear partner can ever move toward weapons-capable fuel. Multi-source (US, India, Middle East Eye); MEE flags the Israeli objection.

stories.label: Trump vows to destroy one Iranian bridge or power plant for every shot Tehran takes at Strait of Hormuz shipping
stories.summary: Trump declared a new red line: for every attack on a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, the US will destroy an Iranian bridge or power plant. Lead with the accountability angle — this openly promises the destruction of civilian infrastructure as reprisal, which is collective punishment under international humanitarian law, not a military target list. The mechanism to teach: a tit-for-tat targeting doctrine tying shipping-lane security to Iranian civilian life. Multi-source (US, India x2); note no Iranian/regional outlet carried this specific vow in the cluster — a feed-side gap to audit.

stories.label: Amnesty: Deadly Pakistan Air Strikes on Kabul Drug Rehab Center a Possible War Crime
stories.summary: Amnesty International found no evidence supporting Pakistan's claim that the Kabul site it bombed on March 16 was a military target — it was a drug rehabilitation center, and the strike may be a war crime. Lead with the named victims and the accountability finding: a named state, a civilian facility, an independent human-rights body assigning responsibility. Teach why the 'military target' claim collapses under Amnesty's evidentiary review. Afghanistan/Pakistan are OIC states; the feed carried no regional (Dawn/Geo) coverage of the Amnesty report — a feed-side gap to note.

stories.label: Israel's Secret Sales Pitch to Provide Surveillance Drones to the UAE
stories.summary: Internal emails and documents show Israel's Elbit Systems working to sell Hermes surveillance drones and other weapons to the UAE. Lead with the accountability scoop: a named arms manufacturer, a documented sales channel, and a Gulf OIC state buying Israeli surveillance tech amid the Gaza genocide. The mechanism to teach — how normalization converts into a concrete weapons-and-surveillance supply chain, visible only through leaked internal records. Original investigative reporting (Drop Site); UAE is OIC, no regional outlet carried the leak.

stories.label: AMD to sell Anthropic tens of billions in AI servers, invest up to $5bn in startup
stories.summary: AMD will sell Anthropic tens of billions in AI servers while simultaneously investing up to $5bn in Anthropic — a 'circular deal' where the chipmaker funds the customer that buys its chips. Lead with the mechanism: this is the same vendor-financing loop Nvidia and OpenAI have built, and it inflates AI capex figures by recycling the same dollars. Teach the reader to spot circular financing as a structural risk in the AI buildout. Regional carry-through: Dawn (PK) is the primary source. No multi-source economy clusters were available in today's feed.

stories.label: S&P Global Ratings upgrades Pakistan's sovereign credit rating to 'B'
stories.summary: S&P raised Pakistan's long-term sovereign rating to 'B' from 'B-' with a stable outlook, citing an improving external position and gradual macro stabilisation. Lead with what an upgrade this deep in the speculative tier actually buys a country on its 25th IMF program: marginally cheaper borrowing, not solvency. Teach the mechanism — how rating tiers gate a fragile economy's access to global capital, and why 'stable' still means junk. Dawn (PK) provides the regional voice for this OIC-state story.

stories.label: Romania faces fuel crisis due to Ukrainian attacks on CPC tankers in Black Sea -- expert
stories.summary: Kazakhstan suspended crude supplies through the Caspian Pipeline Consortium after Ukrainian drone strikes hit tankers near Novorossiysk, and Romania now faces a fuel-market crisis. Lead with the chokepoint mechanism: a landlocked Central Asian OIC producer, a single Black Sea export terminal, and deep-strike drone warfare combine to threaten fuel supply hundreds of km away. Teach how one pipeline-and-port dependency transmits a distant war into a European energy shock. Single Russian state source (TASS) — treat sourcing with caution and seek corroboration in writing.

stories.label: France records 5,764 excess deaths during June heatwave: officials
stories.summary: Public Health France recorded 5,764 excess deaths in the June 17-July 2 heatwave — the highest since the 2003 catastrophe. Lead with the number and the named victims: excess mortality is the clearest measure of a heatwave's human cost, most of it among the elderly. Teach the mechanism of how epidemiologists compute 'excess deaths' against a baseline, and why the metric matters more than the temperature record. TRT World (TR) carries it.

stories.label: Astronomers spot exomoon candidate that's almost as massive as Jupiter
stories.summary: Astronomers may have found the first moon outside our Solar System, orbiting a brown dwarf — but it's nearly as massive as Jupiter, which forces the question of what even counts as a 'moon.' Lead with the definitional puzzle, not just the discovery: the object is so large it blurs the moon/planet boundary. Teach the detection method and why exomoons are so hard to confirm. Nature-published research; The Register gives the reader the technical framing.

stories.label: Flock 'Objects to Our Removing Their Equipment': Emails Reveal Why a Town Put Bags Over Its Flock Cameras
stories.summary: A town wanted to remove its Flock automated license-plate readers; internal emails show the surveillance vendor objected, so the town bagged the cameras instead of taking them down. Lead with the power inversion the emails expose: a private ALPR company asserting a claim over public infrastructure a municipality no longer wants. Teach the mechanism — how vendor contracts lock towns into surveillance networks that are easier to cover than to cancel. Original 404 Media reporting from primary documents.

stories.label: You Opened a Credit Card. ICE Now Knows Where You Live
stories.summary: 404 Media traces the exact path by which a home address from a credit-card application travels through data brokers and ends up in ICE's hands. Lead with the everyday trigger — opening a credit card — and follow the money and data to an enforcement agency. Teach the mechanism the reader can't otherwise see: the commercial data-broker pipeline that converts routine consumer records into deportation-relevant intelligence, with no consent step. Original investigation.

stories.label: New Kimsuky campaign compromised South Korean software vendors
stories.summary: North Korea's Kimsuky APT compromised South Korean vendors of collaborative-work software — a supply-chain foothold, not a single target. Lead with the strategic logic: hitting groupware vendors gives an espionage group downstream access to every organization that runs their software. Teach the reader why software-supply-chain attacks are force multipliers and how state APTs exploit the trust built into vendor update channels. Specialist security reporting (The Record).

stories.label: Libya's New AI Strategy Celebrates Participation, Yet Was Built Without It
stories.summary: Libya's Government of National Unity unveiled a National AI Strategy 2026-2030 and an AI ethics charter that loudly invoke 'participation' — but civil-society groups say they were drafted without any. Lead with the accountability gap: a fractured state announcing AI governance framed around inclusion it never practiced. Teach the reader how AI-strategy documents can launder legitimacy for weak governments, and why who is in the room matters more than the charter's language. SMEX (LB) is the regional digital-rights voice; Libya is an OIC state.

stories.label: Exam paper leaks, protests and Gandhi siblings' arrest -- India's 'cockroach' youth movement explained
stories.summary: The NEET paper leak has metastasised into the biggest street challenge to Modi's third term: a youth-led 'cockroach' movement camped at Jantar Mantar, the arrest of Gandhi siblings, and a paralysed parliament. Lead with the shift in stakes — this is no longer one exam scandal but a generational revolt over blocked mobility, and the government is offering debate, not accountability. Teach the mechanism: a centralised high-stakes exam with weak custody controls turns every leak into a national legitimacy crisis. Multi-perspective (Pakistani, British, Singaporean, Emirati coverage); advances the india-neet arc with a genuinely new development.

stories.label: Apocalyptic fires as Ukraine unleashes hell on Russia's Amazon - £1bn of damage
stories.summary: Strip the tabloid framing and lead with the target logic: Ukraine hit Wildberries warehouses in Krasnodar and Nevinnomyssk — Russia's largest online retailer — citing its links to the war effort, causing more than £1bn in damage. The mechanism to teach is deep-strike economic warfare: with the front frozen, Kyiv is systematically burning the civilian-facing logistics that fund and supply Moscow. Note the sharp sentiment split across the Russian, Ukrainian, Qatari and Indian sources over whether a retail hub is a legitimate military target.

stories.label: The world's deadliest sea crossing – and the role for Australia
stories.summary: Hundreds drowned crossing the Andaman Sea last week — overwhelmingly Rohingya fleeing Myanmar and the camps in Bangladesh — making it again the world's deadliest maritime route. Lead with the named victims and the consequence, not the policy: a stateless Muslim minority is dying at sea because no state in the region will offer safe harbour. Teach the structural gap — ASEAN's existing search-and-rescue and disembarkation tools go unused — and hold regional governments to account for a preventable death toll.

stories.label: Despite governor's executive orders, illegal mining denies Taraba State billions of naira annually
stories.summary: Three executive orders in three years have failed to stop illegal mining in Nigeria's Taraba State, which loses billions of naira annually to unregulated extraction of sapphire and other minerals. Lead with the accountability gap: the governor keeps signing orders that go unenforced while the resource wealth flows out untaxed and untraced. Teach the mechanism — weak custody over mineral rights plus non-enforcement equals a permanent leak from state coffers — and treat West Africa as an economic actor, not a backdrop.

stories.label: Nigerian students lament the delay in NELFUND upkeep allowance
stories.summary: Nigeria's flagship student loan scheme (NELFUND) is failing on its most basic promise: beneficiaries in public universities say the monthly upkeep allowance meant to reduce financial burden has stalled. Lead with who is affected — low-income students who structured their term budgets around a payment that isn't arriving. Teach why loan-plus-stipend schemes live or die on disbursement reliability, and hold the federal fund accountable for the gap between announced policy and money in students' hands.

stories.label: Pakistan and China deepen halal meat trade ties
stories.summary: Pakistan is deepening halal meat exports to China — a concrete instance of South-South trade that lets Islamabad monetise a certified niche while diversifying away from Gulf-dependent revenue. Lead with the economic logic for a chronically debt-stressed economy on its 25th IMF program: halal certification is a tradeable standard, and China is a vast destination market. Teach how the global halal economy functions as an export lever for Muslim-majority producers, and what China's appetite means for Pakistani farmers.

stories.label: Association of an almond-based low-carbohydrate diet with continuous glucose monitoring metrics in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a randomized controlled trial
stories.summary: A randomised controlled trial tracks continuous glucose monitoring metrics in type 2 diabetics on an almond-based low-carbohydrate diet. Lead with the reader-useful finding and the strength of the design — an RCT with CGM, not observational correlation. Teach what the glucose-variability numbers actually show and where the trial's limits are, so a technically literate reader can weigh a widely-hyped dietary claim against real evidence. Diabetes prevalence is rising fastest across South Asia and the Gulf, making the mechanism directly relevant.

stories.label: Security Issues Are Overshadowing Kashmir's Worsening Climate Crisis
stories.summary: Kashmir's Himalayan environment is heating and drying — shrinking glaciers, erratic snowpack, stressed water supply — while the militarised security frame crowds the climate story out of the news entirely. Lead with the physical trend that continues regardless of the political attention it doesn't get. Teach the mechanism: a fragile mountain hydrology feeds the rivers of both India and Pakistan, so a warming Kashmir is a downstream water-security problem for hundreds of millions, not a local weather footnote.

stories.label: In Kyushu's decorated tombs, humans were never meant to be individuals
stories.summary: Sixth-to-seventh-century decorated tombs in Kyushu encode a worldview in which the dead were not individuals but part of a collective — read from the geometry, pigments and orientation of the chambers themselves. Lead with the counter-intuitive claim and the method: how an archaeologist reconstructs a vanished cosmology from stone and darkness. This is editorial taste — a story that teaches the reader something about early Japan and about how material evidence becomes interpretation.

stories.label: Ukrainian drones deliver robots directly into battle by sea and air
stories.summary: Ukraine is now using flying drone-carriers and drone boats to deliver armed ground robots into battle — machines carrying other machines to the fight. Lead with the tactical leap: slow wheeled robots that could never cross contested terrain on their own are being air- and sea-dropped past Russian defences. Teach the reader (a technically literate one) why this composability matters — it turns expendable robots into a deployable system, and it is a preview of how autonomous ground warfare will actually be logistically fought.

stories.label: Israel targets X users, right-wing media with $2 million ad push
stories.summary: Grounded in a new FARA disclosure — documents, not allegation — this maps how Israel paid a Republican-aligned firm (Targeted Communications, a Stagwell subsidiary) ~$9.9M to run pro-Israel influence operations, including ~$2M in ads on X, media bookings on Fox/CNN/NBC, and undisclosed foreign-agent columnists. Lead with the named actors and the paper trail. Teach the mechanism of modern platform influence ops — ad buys, bot amplification, unlabelled TV surrogates — and the accountability gap where one $750k subcontractor is hidden from a transparency statute.

stories.label: The U.S. wants to contain China's AI. Silicon Valley keeps using it
stories.summary: Washington's AI-containment strategy is being quietly undercut from inside: Apple, Thinking Machines and developers worldwide are adopting Chinese open-weight models like Moonshot's Kimi K3 because they are good and cheap. Lead with the contradiction — the same policymakers trying to fence off Chinese AI can't stop US firms from building on it. Teach the mechanism of open-weights diffusion: once a capable model is released openly, export controls on chips can't claw back the software, and the containment premise collapses. Distinct from the 'open-weights winning' framing — the news here is US-side adoption defying policy.

stories.label: Rubio warns Iranian control over Hormuz would set 'very dangerous precedent'
stories.summary: Rubio told ASEAN leaders in Manila that Iran's demand to control and toll the Strait of Hormuz would threaten the world economy and freedom of navigation. Lead with the mechanism, not the soundbite: ~20% of global oil and LNG transits Hormuz, so a tolling regime imposed by a belligerent turns a wartime chokepoint into a permanent tax on Asian and Muslim-world energy importers. Teach why Iran is even in a position to make the demand (11 nights of US strikes, the war reopened) and why the US frames a Gulf waterway as an Asian security problem. Note the sharp sentiment split across the Israeli, Indian, Singaporean and Canadian coverage.

stories.label: Parliament Clash: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha Adjourned Till 2 PM Amid NEET Debate Standoff
stories.summary: India's parliament ground to a halt as the opposition demanded Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resign over a NEET-UG medical-entrance paper leak that has triggered nationwide protests (including the CJP sit-in at Jantar Mantar). Lead with who is affected: millions of students whose one shot at a medical seat was compromised by an exam-mafia leak, and a government offering debate but not accountability. Teach why NEET is such a high-stakes single point of failure in Indian mobility, and why paper leaks recur — the mechanism is a centralized high-stakes exam with weak custody controls, not a one-off scandal.

stories.label: In Southern Lebanon, a Gloss of Diplomacy Can't Hide the Reality of Occupation
stories.summary: A ground report from Majdal Zoun, occupied and depopulated by Israeli forces, overlooking Al-Mansouri where the few remaining residents are shelled almost daily. The angle: while a Trump-brokered framework and Aoun's diplomacy are presented as peace, occupation and daily attacks continue on the ground — continuation of the ẓulm is the development. Name the villages and the residents; teach the gap between the diplomatic narrative and what depopulation and a permanent Israeli presence in south Lebanon actually mean for the people still there.

stories.label: Iran targets 'digital eye' of CENTCOM in Bahrain
stories.summary: Iran's armed forces say they struck Amazon Web Services data infrastructure in Bahrain, calling it the 'digital eye' of US Central Command and a hub for military data analysis. Lead with the systemic exposure, not the claim itself: modern warfighting runs on commercial cloud, so a strike on an AWS region is an attack on both the Pentagon's command loop and the civilian fintech, banking and services across the Gulf and South Asia that share that infrastructure (the same AWS Bahrain region whose disruption has knocked out consumer apps before). Frame it as Iran's stated claim, and teach why militarizing commercial cloud blurs the line between a military target and civilian critical infrastructure.

stories.label: Cost of preparing pot of jollof rice up 14.6% in 11 months - Report
stories.summary: The cost of cooking Nigeria's staple pot of jollof rose 14.6% in 11 months, from N25,798 to a new high, and the report shows how households are absorbing it: smaller quantities, dried substitutes for fresh produce, shrinking portions. Lead with the coping behavior — food inflation measured not as a CPI print but as a family eating less. Teach why a single-dish index (rice, tomatoes, pepper, oil) is a sharper read on Nigerian welfare than headline inflation, and connect it to naira weakness and the broader African food-security squeeze.

stories.label: Bitcoin at $66,300 as yen hits a 40-year low against dollar
stories.summary: Lead with the yen, not bitcoin: the Japanese currency slid to its weakest level since 1986, a 40-year low, signalling deepening stress in the world's third-largest economy as rate divergence with the US widens. Teach the mechanism — a cheap yen makes Japanese exports competitive but imported energy and food dearer, and a disorderly slide risks unwinding the yen-funded carry trades that ripple through global markets. Bitcoin's steadiness near $66,300 is the sidebar (a fixed-supply hedge narrative), not the story.

stories.label: Oil depot in southern Russia's Armavir catches fire following massive drone attack
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike set an oil depot ablaze in Armavir, Krasnodar Region, part of a wider overnight wave (Russia says 242 drones downed, Wildberries logistics centres hit). Lead with the strategy, not the fire: Ukraine is systematically hitting Russian fuel storage and logistics deep behind the front to degrade the war economy — refining throughput, military resupply and export revenue — rather than territory. Teach why energy infrastructure has become the decisive target and how these strikes tighten Russia's domestic fuel supply. Source is Russian state media (TASS); attribute the casualty and interception figures accordingly.

stories.label: 2,000 volunteers join a painstaking effort to restore massive skeleton of prehistoric predator
stories.summary: In a glass-walled lab in Warsaw's Copernicus Science Centre, 2,000 volunteers with chisels and brushes are freeing the bones of a massive prehistoric amphibian from rock. The angle: citizen science at scale — an excavation and preparation task too large for a small professional team, opened to the public as both restoration and education. Teach what the specimen (a large Triassic-era predator) tells us about the ecosystem before dinosaurs dominated, and why fossil preparation, not just discovery, is the real bottleneck in paleontology.

stories.label: UK Misses Deadline to Award Contract for Space Debris Removal Mission
stories.summary: The UK Space Agency blew past its 30 March deadline to award a £75.6M contract for Britain's first active debris-removal mission — capturing and de-orbiting dead satellites. Lead with the accountability gap: everyone agrees low Earth orbit is filling with dangerous junk, yet the actual mission to clean it keeps slipping. Teach why active debris removal is technically hard and commercially unattractive (you must rendezvous with and grab an uncontrolled tumbling object), and why that makes it a public-good problem governments underfund until a Kessler-style collision cascade forces the issue.

stories.label: China's open-weights AI strategy is winning
stories.summary: A widely-shared argument (top of Hacker News, 1,200+ points) that China's bet on open-weights models is beating America's locked-down, proprietary approach. Lead with the mechanism developers care about: open weights can be downloaded, fine-tuned, self-hosted and audited, so they compound adoption and trust in a way API-gated frontier models don't — especially across the Global South and cost-sensitive builders. Teach the strategic stakes for the reader: whose models become the default substrate of the next decade is a question of distribution and openness, not just benchmark scores, and export controls may be accelerating the very outcome they meant to prevent.

stories.label: Self-healing and adhesive eutectogel with skin-like softness and toughness for durable ionic skins
stories.summary: Researchers built a self-healing, adhesive gel (a eutectogel) that is soft and tough like skin and conducts ions, aimed at durable 'ionic skins' for wearables and soft robots. Lead with the durability problem it solves: e-skins normally tear, dry out and lose conductivity, so a material that autonomously re-bonds after damage is what makes long-lived skin-like sensors plausible. Teach the trick in plain terms — a hydrogen-bond-rich deep-eutectic solvent acts as both the medium and a reversible physical crosslinker — and why soft, self-repairing conductors matter for prosthetics, health monitoring and human-machine interfaces.

stories.label: Could This New Northrop Spacecraft Use Its Robotic Arms To Attack Enemy Satellites?
stories.summary: Northrop's Mission Robotic Vehicle is built to grab, service and refuel satellites in orbit with robotic arms — but the same capability that repairs a satellite can disable or move an enemy one. Lead with the dual-use hinge: on-orbit servicing and counterspace weapons are physically the same technology, separated only by intent. Teach the reader why this collapses any clean line between peaceful orbital robotics and ASAT capability, why it's near-impossible to verify from the ground, and how it accelerates the militarization of orbit without a single missile launch.
